title: The portal
place: In the lane, a few steps back from the main portal, facing it.

pano.note: Flat stand-in until a real 360 source is confirmed

find.prompt: Find it: tap the medallion at the foot of the left-hand niche.
find.answer: One medallion was carved; its twin was only drawn, still waiting for a chisel.

quiz.q: Why is the portal turned 17° out from the wall?
options: To be seen from the Citadel
quiz.why: It was angled so it could be seen from the sultan's palace on the Citadel hill.

onsite.stand: Stand in the lane a few steps back from the main portal and face it.

lineTags.2: Unverified on site: the Citadel's direction from here. The 17 degrees and 'most likely to be seen from the Citadel': Wikipedia, after Behrens-Abouseif
lineTags.3: Dramatised: the sultan watching his portal from the Citadel is invented; the portal was turned to face the Citadel: Wikipedia, after Behrens-Abouseif
lineTags.4: Portal nearly 38 m high (Behrens-Abouseif via Wikipedia; Williams gives 36 m for the building) and the muqarnas hood: Wikipedia
lineTags.5: Two tall niches, and black marble panels with white Kufic of Surat al-Fath (the Sura of Victory): Wikipedia
lineTags.6: Dramatised: Bashir's presence at the carving is invented; the method (a master draws, apprentices cut) is what scholars think likely (Wikipedia, Williams 2018). The minaret over the door: al-Maqrizi, Khitat
lineTags.7: Four minarets planned, the one over the door fell and its twin was never built: al-Maqrizi, Khitat. The ghost minaret is a reconstruction by the MEDU 3D model, not a record
lineTags.9: About 300 dead, orphans of the sabil school among them: al-Maqrizi, Khitat
lineTags.10: al-Maqrizi, Khitat, his own words, abridged; 'Misr' here is Fustat
lineTags.12: Killed 33 days after the fall; never rebuilt: al-Maqrizi, Khitat
lineTags.13: Bashir al-Jamdar finished the marble: al-Maqrizi, Khitat
lineTags.14: Unverified: which niche holds the medallion
lineTags.15: One medallion carved, its twin only outlined: Wikipedia, after Behrens-Abouseif
